title: The Microbiome in Uveitis and Pediatric Inflammatory Diseases
official: The Gut Microbiota in Uveitis and Pediatric Inflammatory Diseases: Identification of the Fecal Peptidoglycan Signature
summary: Chronic, noninfectious uveitis in children, associated with various systemic inflammatory diseases, carries a high risk of vision loss. Intestinal dysbiosis and the translocation of bacterial peptidoglycans (PG) that activate innate receptors recognizing PG could represent a common initiating mechanism, independent of the underlying disease. Studying these biological signatures in comparative cohorts could lead to a better understanding of the onset of uveitis and the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients under the age of 18 being treated at Robert-Debré Hospital
* Patients being treated for noninfectious uveitis, or with pediatric inflammatory diseases without uveitis (connective tissue disorders, granulomatosis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, pediatric vasculitides).
* The child and his or her parents have no objection to participating in the study
* Siblings of patients (family controls) or other healthy controls (children of hospital staff)
